title: As, Bowed by Sudden Storms, the Rose
description: As, Bowed by Sudden Storms, the Rose in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Lydia Sigourney wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 579 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Burial of a Friend”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: As, bowed by sud-den storms, the rose Sinks on the gar-den's breast, Down to the grave our bro-ther goes, In si-lence there to rest.

lines: As, bowed by sudden storms, the rose
Down to the grave our brother goes,
No more with us his tuneful voice
The hymn of praise shall swell;
No more his cheerful heart rejoice
Yet, if, in yonder cloudless sphere
He utters in his Saviour's ear
No more we'll mourn the absent friend,
To rise and join him there.

licence: Public domain: Lydia Sigourney died in 1865.
credits: Words by Lydia Sigourney (1791–1865), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
